newsitem.title: UK: London gold fixes firmer, PGMs continue surge.
newsitem.headline: London gold fixes firmer, PGMs continue surge.

text.p: Gold and silver prices moved higher on Thursday but still lagged behind the surging platinum group metal (PGMs) markets where huge fresh gains were recorded.
Platinum was fixed at its highest level since August 23, 1990 and palladium established a fresh high since March 1980 in markets were lack of supplies was squeezing prices up daily, dealers said.

Gold was fixed at $343.80 per ounce, up three dollars from Thursday afternoon. Platinum was fixed at $495.00 and palladium at $240.00 its highest fix since twice-daily fixing of the metal began in 1989.
"There was been some switching of interest to gold and silver today as speculators tried to get them up on the back of palladium," one dealer said.

Platinum and especially palladium prices have boomed this year due to leading supplier Russia failing to export since last December due to administrative problems. The resultant market shortage has caused a scramble for scarce metal and attracted speculative investment funds to the markets.
The London Platinum and Palladium Market Association met late on Thursday to review the conditions which had led to talk of legal action and rumours of major defaults and losses.
"The members confirmed that there were no defaults in the market," said Trevor Pitts, association chairman.
Unusually wide buy-sell spreads of $30 against $1.00 normally has made trading in platinum extremely risky.
"We have seen vastly more business being done on the fixing as dealers try to avoid the price risk involved in these spreads," Pitts said.,"

"We called the meeting in response to concerns about the tightness in the market...The members agreed to try to offer clients an orderly market. The key issue really depends on when the Russians begin exporting again," Pitts said.
Dealers had stopped quoting forward rates for palladium after the cost of borrowing it surged to around 300 percent for one-month metal. Now they will only do so on a "suggestion" basis, Pitts said.
Russian officials negotiating contracts in Tokyo have said June 20 was a likely start date.
Dealers said silver could be the next precious metal to make a move higher. It was quoted at $4.91/$4.93, up 16 cents.
"There are some (buy) stops on Comex that they will try to hit when New York opens and that could start a run. It could go much higher," a dealer said. --Brian Spoors +44 171 542 8058
